title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

reading.body:
A fleet of Waymo autonomous vehicles became immobilized on San Francisco streets during Fourth of July celebrations when their batteries depleted while the cars sat in traffic congestion. The vehicles, primarily Jaguar I-PACE models, had no means to navigate out of the gridlock or reach charging infrastructure while stationary. The system was deployed into conditions it was not built to handle: prolonged unexpected traffic caused by major city events, road closures, and high volume that exceeded its battery endurance during idle operation.

This failure occurred in the deployment layer rather than the AI model itself. The vehicles lacked either sufficient battery capacity for foreseeable congestion, dynamic rerouting that might have avoided the gridlock, or integration with traffic prediction systems that could have warned operators in advance. Catching it would have required stress-testing the autonomous fleet against historical traffic patterns during major San Francisco events and ensuring sufficient buffers in battery management for degraded conditions.

It is not established whether the fire from a fireworks device represents a failure of the autonomous system's fire detection or response capabilities, nor whether this incident led to specific operational changes beyond Waymo's stated evaluation of resilience measures.

reports.title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

summary:
Several Waymo autonomous vehicles became stranded on San Francisco streets during Fourth of July celebrations after their batteries depleted while stuck in heavy traffic. Video footage showed at least a dozen Waymo vehicles, primarily Jaguar I-PACE models, lined up stationary on streets following a fireworks display at the Golden Gate Bridge. The company attributed the situation to major traffic disruptions, high traveler volume, and unexpected road closures. One vehicle caught fire after driving over fireworks someone had set off, though no injuries were reported. Frustrated motorists spent extended periods in gridlock as Waymo's roadside assistance team worked to clear the vehicles.

Waymo stated it is evaluating ways to improve resilience during major traffic disruptions. The incident prompted San Francisco officials to review the situation, with Mayor Daniel Lurie's office announcing plans to hold conversations with public and private partners about Saturday's congestion. This represents another challenge for Waymo operations in San Francisco, following a December incident when over 100 of its vehicles stopped at intersections during a citywide power outage that disabled traffic lights.
